claim.pdf_says: Format 1 (to-message-server): 'SEND TO { literal-1 / message-server-name-1 } FROM identifier-1' -- at 300 dpi (crop of the printed glyphs, and again for Format 2 'SEND TO  data-name-2  FROM identifier-1') the underline rule runs only beneath SEND and beneath FROM. There is a clear gap after the D of SEND and NO rule beneath TO in either format. (By contrast the SET formats on pp. 759-762 do print an underline beneath TO, so the omission here is deliberate typesetting, not a printing defect.)
claim.markdown_says: ISO_COBOL.md line 30641 (Format 1 figure note): '... Underlined (required) words: SEND, TO, FROM, RETURNING, EXCEPTION, NOT, END-SEND.'  and line 30658 (Format 2 figure note): '... Underlined (required) words: SEND, TO, FROM, RAISING, EXCEPTION, LAST, NOT, END-SEND.'
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2 an underlined word is a REQUIRED word; a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word that may be omitted without changing meaning. Both SEND figure notes promote the optional word TO to required. A compiler implemented from this transcription would reject legal source such as SEND "SRV" FROM WS-MSG RETURNING WS-TAG ... END-SEND (TO omitted) -- the same falsely-restrictive direction as the known choice-indicator losses. The choice-indicator bars and every other claim in these two notes are correct; only the TO entry is wrong.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct pixel measurement of the 300 dpi render of spec_p756.png (2550x3300), not by eye alone.

FORMAT 1 (14.9.38.2, printed page 726 = PDF page 756). Glyph-group x-extents on the 'SEND TO { ... } FROM identifier-1' line (ink columns, y 1075-1112): SEND=(305,406), TO=(424,474), brace=(509,519), FROM=(1086,1197), identifier-1=(1215,1399). Scanning the underline band (y 1080-1130) for horizontal dark runs >=25 px returns EXACTLY TWO rules, both on rows y=1114 and y=1115: x=(306,404) and x=(1088,1195). Those align to the pixel with SEND and with FROM. Nothing whatsoever exists in the TO span (424,474) on the underline row. (The only other long runs in the band, at y=1120, x=(562,589) and (923,950), are the horizontal arms of the { } braces, not rules.)

FORMAT 2. Glyph groups on the 'SEND TO  data-name-2  FROM identifier-1' line (y 1755-1792): SEND=(318,419), TO=(438,487), data-name-2=(525,760), FROM=(789,900), identifier-1=(919,1128). Underline band again yields exactly two rules, rows y=1794/1795: x=(320,417) and x=(791,898) -- SEND and FROM only. The TO span (438,487) is bare.

The rules under SEND and FROM are detected as 2-px-tall runs on the same two scan rows, which establishes that the scan is sensitive enough to see a rule of that weight; an underline beneath TO would necessarily share that baseline and would have been detected. Its absence is real, not a thresholding artifact.

DEFECT-vs-CONVENTION CONTROL. Rendered PDF page 759 (printed 729, 14.9.39 SET statement) as a control: SET Format 1 prints 'SET { index-name-1 / identifier-1 } ... TO { ... }' with TO clearly underlined, and Format 3 prints 'SET { {mnemonic-name-1} ... TO { ON / OFF } } ...' likewise with TO underlined. The same typesetting run therefore does underline TO where TO is a keyword, so the p.756 omission is deliberate, exactly as the claim states.

MARKDOWN QUOTATION VERIFIED VERBATIM. sed -n '30641p;30658p' specs/ISO_COBOL.md reproduces both figure notes character-for-character as quoted, each ending 'Underlined (required) words: SEND, TO, FROM, ...'. This is not reflow, wrapping, page-break furniture, or a formatting artifact: the transcription's fenced code block cannot carry underlining, so the figure note IS the sole carrier of the required/optional distinction, and that carrier states the opposite of the printed page for TO.

NORMATIVE EFFECT VERIFIED AGAINST THE CONVENTION CLAUSES. 5.2.2 Keywords: 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword'. 5.2.3 Optional words: 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity ...'. So the non-underlined TO is an optional word and 'SEND literal-1 FROM identifier-1 RETURNING data-name-1 ... END-SEND' with TO omitted is legal source. I also scanned 14.9.38.3 syntax rules and 14.9.38.4 general rules for any rule reinstating TO as mandatory: none exists (the rules discuss literal-1, message-server-name-1, identifier-1, data-name-2 and the RAISING/ON EXCEPTION phrases only). The error is therefore falsely restrictive in the same direction as the known choice-indicator losses.

ADVERSARIAL CHECKS THAT FAILED TO REFUTE: (a) the text is not merely reflowed onto an adjacent line -- the assertion 'TO is underlined' appears nowhere correct on the page; (b) the claim does not misquote either source; (c) the difference does change meaning (required vs optional word); (d) the remainder of both notes checks out against the glyphs -- ON is printed WITHOUT an underline while NOT and EXCEPTION are underlined, RAISING and LAST are underlined, the ON/NOT ON EXCEPTION bracket does carry choice-indicator bars just inside it, and the RAISING brace carries no bars. So the notes' authors did understand the convention; TO is an isolated slip, not a systemic misreading.

SWEEP FOR SIBLINGS: grep -o 'Underlined \(required\) words:[^.]*\bTO\b' over specs/ISO_COBOL.md returns exactly two hits, lines 30641 and 30658 -- both on this page. No other figure note in the transcription wrongly lists TO as underlined.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, and the claim is accurate as written apart from one citation slip. Printed page 756 (ISO printed folio 726), 14.9.38.2 SEND general formats: in BOTH Format 1 (to-message-server) and Format 2 (message-server-response) the underline rule is present only beneath SEND and beneath FROM -- pixel-verified at 300 dpi, rules at y=1114/1115 spanning x=(306,404) and (1088,1195) in Format 1 and at y=1794/1795 spanning x=(320,417) and (791,898) in Format 2, versus TO occupying x=(424,474) and (438,487) respectively with no ink on the underline row. TO is therefore an OPTIONAL word in the SEND statement. The transcription's two figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 30641 and 30658 both list TO in 'Underlined (required) words:', promoting an optional word to a keyword. Because the fenced ASCII figure cannot render underlining, the note is the only place the required/optional distinction survives, so the error is fully load-bearing: a compiler built from the transcription would reject legal source such as SEND "SRV" FROM WS-MSG RETURNING WS-TAG END-SEND. FIX: delete 'TO, ' from both lists, and preferably add an explicit sentence to each note, e.g. 'TO and ON are printed WITHOUT an underline -- they are optional words.' CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM'S RATIONALE ONLY (does not affect the verdict): the underlining convention is not 5.2.6.2 (5.2.6 is 'Options'); it is 5.2.2 Keywords ('shown in uppercase and underlined ... They are required') together with 5.2.3 Optional words ('shown in uppercase and not underlined ... may be written to add clarity'). The claim's control observation is also confirmed: PDF page 759 (SET Formats 1 and 3) prints TO underlined, so p.756 is deliberate typesetting rather than a printing defect. Everything else asserted by the two notes matches the printed glyphs (ON not underlined; NOT, EXCEPTION, RETURNING, RAISING, LAST underlined; choice-indicator bars present inside the ON/NOT ON EXCEPTION bracket and absent from the RAISING brace). A sweep of the whole transcription finds this TO error only on these two lines.
